results.answer: Launchpad runs as connected levels. (1) Launchpad Foundations — an entry summer program in core AI and technical skills. (2) Launchpad 101 — a yearlong, learn-and-earn program for high school juniors and seniors, four afternoons a week with summer intensives, where students earn stipends, complete paid internships, and earn industry certifications (e.g. Certiport Generative AI Foundations); it offers two pathways, Software Development and Entrepreneurial Leadership, so students not drawn to coding still build real AI/STEM skills. (3) LiftOff — a six-month, full-time, AI-first software-development track for graduates ready to go deeper (participants 18–24), with a guaranteed $6,000 stipend floor over six months plus wraparound supports (transportation, food, a laptop, and coaching). (4) Launchpad Inc. — a nonprofit social enterprise, now the second half of LiftOff, that puts participants on paid client projects at $20/hour for local nonprofits, foundations, and small businesses. Participants train against Launchpad's AI Engineer competency framework — six competencies and 24 skills, staged Associate → AI Engineer (Junior is the graduation bar) — assessed on deployed work rather than seat time and tracked in Beacon, Building 21's competency and data platform.

results.answer: Launchpad builds accelerated pathways that connect Philadelphia young adults to high-paying, future-ready tech careers. Through a paid AI-engineering program grounded in real client work, participants who arrive with a high school diploma and little else gain applied AI skills, industry certifications, a portfolio of deployed work, and the paid experience employers now demand — at no cost to them — on a path toward a $50,000 living wage.

results.answer: Launchpad recruits Philadelphia young people from more than 30 non-selective high schools and across 30+ ZIP codes, no prior experience required, and pays them from day one so finishing is financially possible. The advanced phases most funders support are LiftOff — six months of full-time, AI-first software-development training for participants 18–24 — and Launchpad Inc., a nonprofit social enterprise that puts participants on real, paid client projects ($20/hour) building automations, dashboards, integrations, and agents for Philadelphia nonprofits and small businesses. Participants train against the AI Engineer competency framework (six competencies, 24 skills; prompting and context engineering, building automations and agents, connecting systems, structuring data, evaluating AI output, and managing cost and risk), earn industry certifications (Generative AI Foundations, PCEP), and are assessed on deployed work tracked in Beacon, so every graduate finishes with a portfolio of shipped AI systems and the client references early-career tech hiring now screens on. Wraparound supports — a guaranteed $6,000 stipend floor, transportation, food, a laptop, and Career Success Coaching that continues through the first year of employment — remove the barriers that otherwise force low-income young adults to drop out. Delivered at no cost from Launchpad's Center City hub at 801 Market Street.

results.answer: Equity is the design. Launchpad recruits from non-selective Philadelphia high schools that do not offer computer science, requires no prior experience, and pays participants so access to a high-paying tech career does not depend on which school a student attended or whether they can afford to train unpaid. The service population is about 85% Black or Brown, nearly 90% low-income, and 100% free/reduced-lunch eligible. Because fewer than 10% of recruited students are initially drawn to software engineering, Launchpad built the Entrepreneurial Leadership pathway so the other ~90% — including many young women who do not see themselves in a coding-only program — reach the same AI skills, paid projects, and credentials. Reaching young women in software specifically remains an active recruitment focus.

results.answer: Launchpad works with 17–20 employer partners who inform the curriculum, host paid placements, sit on the advisory board, and run mock interviews and portfolio reviews — including Accenture (hosted the Cohort 1 graduation), Seer Interactive (hired a graduate over 200+ applicants, then more), Bentley Systems, CreateAccess (converted an intern to a permanent role), Hack Club, HiTouch Enterprises, AECOM, Nerd Street, PGW, and PECO. Through Launchpad Inc., participants have delivered paid client work for Philadelphia nonprofits and civic organizations including North10 Philadelphia, the Share Food Program, and Rock to the Future. Launchpad partners with more than 30 Philadelphia high schools for recruitment, relies on parent organization Building 21 for the competency-based model and the Beacon platform, and has a dual-enrollment partnership with Mastery Charter School. A standing committee of industry professionals shapes the curriculum to what employers hire for.

items.note: The platform records a Lightspeed phase that the KB program descriptions omit entirely, so a drafted program description built only from the KB is missing a phase. Queried 2026-08-11 — Lightspeed is a 7-week summer intensive, run twice: 2024-07-01 to 2024-08-19 (7 completers) and 2025-07-07 to 2025-08-27 (8), 15 of 15 completing and none dropping. 14 of the 15 sat PCEP and all 14 passed. Do NOT describe it as a linear stage between 101 and LiftOff: it runs in the summer gap between school years, no student has it as current_phase, and its completers show up later under LiftOff and Alumni. Use query_enrollment active_during with phase=Lightspeed and a wide date window for the roster — by_phase gives only the counts, and by_student cannot filter by phase at all (see the filter caveat in CLAUDE.md §4).
